### What is the meaning of the meta estimation error? {#what-is-the-meaning-of-the-meta-estimation-error .revision-section}

[REPLACED SECTION · 18 October 2026]{.revision-label}

The concern I raised in my email to Sra is simple: **there are not enough restrictions on $\theta_i$ to force a nonzero intra-document estimation error. We can always choose $\theta_i=\psi$.** At the other extreme, we can choose $\theta_i=D_i$. Both choices preserve the distribution of the documents, but give different meanings to the paper's error terms.

#### The two choices: $\theta_i=\psi$ and $\theta_i=D_i$

One sample is **one complete document**, $D_i\in\Sigma^T$. Tokens within that document need not be independent. Keep the shared parameter $\psi$ and the joint law of the documents fixed, with $D_1,D_2,\ldots$ iid conditional on $\psi$. Write $C_M=(D_1,\ldots,D_M)$ and $Q=P(D_i\in\cdot\mid\psi)$.

The paper's Theorem Jeon.4.2, together with its irreducible baseline, gives

$$
\underbrace{\frac{H(C_M)}{MT}}_{\substack{\text{optimal}\\\text{log-loss}}}
=\underbrace{
\underbrace{\frac{I(C_M;\psi)}{MT}}_{\substack{\text{meta}\\\text{estimation error}}}
+\underbrace{\frac{I(D_i;\theta_i\mid\psi)}{T}}_{\substack{\text{intra-document}\\\text{estimation error}}}
}_{\text{estimation error}}
+\underbrace{\frac{H(D_i\mid\theta_i)}{T}}_{\substack{\text{irreducible}\\\text{error}}}.
$$

**Choice 1: $\theta_i=\psi$.** Give every document parameter exactly the shared information. Given $\psi$, choose the sole available parameter $\theta_i=\psi$, then generate the complete document from $Q$. This is precisely the original conditional document distribution, with any former document-specific latent variable integrated out. Now

$$
\underbrace{I(D_i;\theta_i\mid\psi)}_{\text{intra-document information}}
=I(D_i;\psi\mid\psi)=0,
\qquad H(D_i\mid\theta_i)=H(D_i\mid\psi).
$$

**Choice 2: $\theta_i=D_i$.** Given $\psi$, draw a document-valued parameter $\theta_i\sim Q$, then output $D_i=\theta_i$. The document has exactly the same law as before, but knowing its parameter now determines it completely:

$$
\underbrace{I(D_i;\theta_i\mid\psi)}_{\text{intra-document information}}
=I(D_i;D_i\mid\psi)=H(D_i\mid\psi),
\qquad H(D_i\mid\theta_i)=0.
$$

These are alternative latent representations. An invertible reparameterization alone cannot change mutual information.

#### Do the paper's assumptions allow this?

Yes, under the general requirements of Section 4.1. Here is the check from my attachment, with its autoregressive step repaired:

| Requirement | $\theta_i=\psi$ | $\theta_i=D_i$ |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Exchangeable documents, iid given $\psi$ | The joint law of $(\psi,D_1,D_2,\ldots)$ stays fixed. | The same conditional law $Q$ is sampled independently for each document. |
| $\theta_1,\theta_2,\ldots\mid\psi$ iid | $\psi,\psi,\ldots\mid\psi$ are iid: a point mass is allowed. | The parameters are independent draws from $Q$. |
| $D_i\perp\psi\mid\theta_i$ | $D_i\perp\psi\mid\psi$. | $D_i\perp\psi\mid D_i$. |
| Autoregressive generation; discrete tokens and length $T$ | Generate from $Q$ using its token conditionals. | Emit the stored document token by token. |
| Independence across documents given $\psi$ | Use independent document draws. | Use independent parameter draws. |

<details class="assumption-check">
<summary>Technical detail: autoregressive generation and the attachment's gap</summary>

For finite $\Sigma$, every document law $r$ on $\Sigma^T$ has an autoregressive generator. If $r[h]$ denotes the probability of prefix $h$, use

$$
A_r(h)(x)=\begin{cases}
r[hx]/r[h],&r[h]>0,\\
1/|\Sigma|,&r[h]=0.
\end{cases}
$$

This reproduces $r$; zero-probability prefixes are never reached. Apply it to $r=Q$ in the first choice and $r=\delta_{\theta_i}$ in the second. On standard Borel parameter spaces these finite sums and piecewise ratios are measurable. No encoding of infinite sequences or differential entropy is needed.

The attachment's item (ii) demanded strict dependence at every token position. De Finetti does not establish that: it concerns independence **across documents**, not dependence inside a document. The paper's Section 3 says the next token “may depend” on the parameter and history; its general framework states no strict information inequality excluding these endpoints. The check above uses conditional kernels instead of that extra premise. The description of parameters as document-specific would need an additional formal restriction to exclude $\theta_i=\psi$.

</details>

#### What follows for the interpretation?

The two choices leave the meta term and optimal log-loss unchanged. They move the entire quantity $H(D_i\mid\psi)/T$ between intra-document estimation error and irreducible error. **If the irreducible error were held fixed as well, this move would be impossible.**

This is the issue behind the question in my email: *is there a missing modeling assumption, or a limitation on the interpretability of the results?* Theorem Jeon.4.2 remains a valid identity. But its intra-document term alone cannot describe a property of the document distribution independently of how $\theta_i$ is chosen.

The same qualification matters for Theorem Jeon.4.7 and Remark Jeon.4.8, which interpret the in-context term as dominant when the meta term is small. With $\theta_i=\psi$, that in-context term is zero. This does not imply that context is useless: the oracle knowing $\psi$ can still exploit dependencies between tokens. It changes the baseline against which estimation error is measured. Further restrictions on $\theta_i$ are needed to give this term the intended meaning. The specialized transformer-mixture assumptions in Theorem Jeon.4.5 would require a separate check.

#### Lemma B.1: the canonical de Finetti split

Fix the law of an **infinite exchangeable sequence of complete documents** on the finite space $\Sigma^T$. Let $Q$ be its de Finetti directing distribution, so documents are iid conditional on $Q$. Then the split

$$
\frac{H(C_M)}{MT}
=\underbrace{\frac{I(C_M;Q)}{MT}}_{\substack{\text{estimation of the}\\\text{shared document distribution}}}
+\underbrace{\frac{H(D_i\mid Q)}{T}}_{\substack{\text{document uncertainty}\\\text{remaining given }Q}}
$$

is determined by that document process. With the canonical choice $\theta_i=\psi=Q$, these are precisely **estimation error** and **irreducible error**, respectively.

**Proof.** The entropy identity and conditional iid property give

$$
H(C_M)=I(C_M;Q)+H(C_M\mid Q)
=I(C_M;Q)+M\mathbb E[h(Q)],
$$

where $h(Q)$ is the entropy of the document distribution. De Finetti's mixing law is unique, so the document process fixes $\mathbb E[h(Q)]$ and hence both terms. Any other shared variable $\psi$ making the infinite document sequence conditionally iid induces the same mixing law through $Q_\psi=P(D_i\in\cdot\mid\psi)$. Therefore $H(C_M\mid\psi)=M\mathbb E[h(Q)]$ and $I(C_M;\psi)=I(C_M;Q)$. $\square$

The uniqueness requires the infinite exchangeable law, not a finite corpus alone; see [Theorem 1 of Barber, Candès, Ramdas, and Tibshirani](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~ryantibs/papers/defin.pdf). **One document is one sample**; nothing here assumes iid tokens inside a document.

Introducing extra document parameters $\theta_i$ splits the second term further:

$$
\frac{H(D_i\mid Q)}{T}
=\underbrace{\frac{I(D_i;\theta_i\mid Q)}{T}}_{\text{intra-document estimation error}}
+\underbrace{\frac{H(D_i\mid\theta_i)}{T}}_{\text{irreducible error}},
$$

provided $D_i\perp Q\mid\theta_i$. The sum is canonical; this further split is not. This is exactly the freedom illustrated by $\theta_i=Q$ and $\theta_i=D_i$ above.

<details class="assumption-check">
<summary>Optional extension: every intermediate allocation</summary>

Independently for each document, choose the second construction with probability $\alpha$ and the first with probability $1-\alpha$. More explicitly, draw $B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\alpha)$ independently of $\psi$. If $B_i=0$, set $\theta_i=(0,\psi)$ and sample $D_i\sim Q$. If $B_i=1$, sample $Z_i\sim Q$, set $\theta_i=(1,Z_i)$, and output $D_i=Z_i$. The tags distinguish the two parameter spaces.

Both branches produce law $Q$, and independent repetition preserves every corpus law, $P(C_M=(d_1,\ldots,d_M))=\mathbb E[\prod_i Q(d_i)]$. The parameters are iid conditional on $\psi$. The requirement $D_i\perp\psi\mid\theta_i$ holds because the first branch specifies $\psi$ and the second specifies $D_i$ itself. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\underbrace{\frac{H(D_i\mid\theta_i)}{T}}_{\text{irreducible error}}
&=(1-\alpha)\frac{H(D_i\mid\psi)}{T},\\[1em]
\underbrace{\frac{I(D_i;\theta_i\mid\psi)}{T}}_{\text{intra-document estimation error}}
&=\alpha\frac{H(D_i\mid\psi)}{T}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first equality averages the conditional entropy of the two branches; the second follows from $I(D_i;\theta_i\mid\psi)=H(D_i\mid\psi)-H(D_i\mid\theta_i)$. This gives every allocation between the endpoints, without relying on the earlier formal proof sheet.

</details>
